analysis:
The ProviderLoop.swift change only adds stored state to the ProviderLoop actor. At head lines 781-792 it adds selectedModelRecovery, selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride (a test-only load closure, nil in production), savedEnabledModels and enabledModelsAtLastSwitch. At line 954 savedEnabledModels is initialised from config.config.backend.enabledModels. I saw no new network input, key handling, decryption, attestation or authorization path, and no change to plaintext handling, coordinator wire behavior, or App Attest or serving-authorization state (TB-002, TB-011, A-016). The new test override is an internal, non-public seam. Its production default is nil, but I did not see the code that consumes it. The saved-selection fields are config-derived values and do not widen what is advertised or served in this diff. The related threat is the model-load and availability class (T-029, T-016), with residual uncertainty about the recovery logic.

Open integration questions for the next pass, since the logic lives in files not supplied:
- ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery: does the no-eviction recovery load go through the same advertised-set guard, self-test and weight-hash capture, and respect admission, drain, update and add-on hold states (TB-012, T-059)? Does it avoid reloading a model retired by a failed self-test (failedSelfTestHashes, retiringModels)?
- Is the policy refresh's read of enabled_models from the config file treated as an operator-owned input, with the running selection changing only at a start or a committed switch?
- Could the recovery load bypass the KV budget or memory-reserve gating?
These are unverified contracts rather than evidenced regressions, so I report no finding. This diff alone shows nothing security-relevant.
